answer: A deposit-backed identity registry makes each agent lock a refundable stake before it can transact. Creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every one ties up real value, like forging a ferrous relic that cannot be mass-produced cheaply. Misbehavior triggers slashing, so the stake is lost, and a plume of suspicious accounts all funded from one source is easy to spot and freeze. Honest agents keep their deposit and build history, while attackers pay per identity and gain nothing.
